html:
Togoland was a protectorate of Germany in West Africa from 1884 to 1914, covering today's Togo and part of eastern Ghana. The map shows it in 1914.

The explorer Gustav Nachtigal signed treaties with coastal chiefs in 1884, and Germany pushed inland in the following years. Germans called it a "model colony" because it paid for itself, with railways from Lome carrying palm products, cocoa and cotton. That income relied on heavy taxes and forced labour.

In August 1914, at the start of World War I, British troops from the Gold Coast and French troops from Dahomey overran it in a few weeks. In 1922 the League of Nations split it into British and French mandates. British Togoland voted in 1956 to join Ghana, which became independent the next year, and French Togoland became Togo in 1960.
sum: Togoland was a protectorate of Germany in West Africa from 1884 to 1914, covering today's Togo and part of eastern Ghana. The map shows it in 1914.
